modules.name: shared-types
owns: CreateLeaveRequestInput DTO (leaveTypeCode, startDate, endDate as ISO strings)

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Extend IApiClient + ApiClient with write endpoints
recommended_phases.rationale: Foundation for everything else. Add createLeave/submitLeave/approveLeave/rejectLeave/cancelLeave to IApiClient and ApiClient using the existing request<T> pattern (bearer token, ApiError mapping, ISO-string dates). No other module can proceed until the transport supports writes.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Extend ILeaveService + LeaveService with write methods
recommended_phases.rationale: Thin delegation layer over the API client. Add create/submit/approve/reject/cancel plus the pure getAvailableLeaveActions and validateLeaveRequestInput helpers. Depends only on Phase 1 and shared-types.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — RequestLeavePage form + route wiring
recommended_phases.rationale: New form page capturing leave type, start/end dates; client-side validation (both dates required, end >= start, type chosen); surfaces API error message on rejection; navigates to detail on success. Depends on Phase 2.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — LeaveDetailPage actions + role awareness
recommended_phases.rationale: Render submit/cancel (owner) and approve/reject (manager) only when available per status+role; refresh status after action without reload; forbidden actions never rendered. Depends on Phase 2 and employee profile.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5 — LeaveListPage link + composition root wiring
recommended_phases.rationale: Add "Request leave" link from list; wire new page into App routes and main.tsx. Depends on Phases 3-4.

app_notes: Web-only feature; no backend/src changes. Layer boundaries: presentation (pages/guards) -> application (modules/* services) -> infrastructure (api-client) -> shared-types. Dependencies flow inward only; no module depends on presentation. The leave module owns the write service methods and two pure helpers (getAvailableLeaveActions for the status+role action matrix, validateLeaveRequestInput for pre-send validation). Role awareness comes from the already-fetched EmployeeProfile (GET /employees/me), never from decoding the JWT in the browser. Dates cross the wire as ISO strings (CreateLeaveRequestInput uses ISO strings; the ApiClient serializes them, never Date objects). The action matrix: owner (request.employeeId === profile.id) may submit/cancel a DRAFT/SUBMITTED request; a MANAGER/ADMIN may approve/reject a SUBMITTED request (manager must be the requester's direct manager per backend, but the client renders the button based on role+status and lets the backend enforce the direct-manager rule, surfacing its 403 as an error). Forbidden actions are never rendered. After a successful action the page re-fetches the request (no manual reload).

open_questions.question: Should the client-side "end date not before start date" validation compare calendar dates only, or also enforce the backend's min-notice / max-duration rules before sending?
open_questions.impact: The feature spec only requires end >= start, both dates required, and a type chosen. Enforcing notice/duration client-side would duplicate backend policy and risk drift; leaving them out means the backend rejects and the form surfaces the API error. This affects the validateLeaveRequestInput helper's scope and the RequestLeavePage test matrix.
candidate_options: Client validates only the three spec'd rules (end >= start, both required, type chosen); backend enforces notice/duration and the form surfaces its error
Client also mirrors min-notice and max-duration using fetched policy data (adds a policy fetch dependency and drift risk)

open_questions.question: For the approve/reject action, should the manager be able to enter an approval comment, and if so is it sent to the backend?
open_questions.impact: The backend approve/reject endpoints currently take no body (the service sets approverId/decidedAt but approvalComment stays null). The feature spec does not mention a comment field. Adding one would require a backend change, which is out of scope; omitting it means the detail page shows "—" for approval comment after a decision.
candidate_options: No comment input; approve/reject are comment-less (matches current backend contract)
Add a comment input that is captured but not sent (misleading, rejected)
Add a comment input and extend the backend (out of scope for this web-only feature)

auth_contract: No new API surface is created by this feature (it consumes existing backend endpoints), so no new auth contract is introduced. The client relies on the existing session: AuthSession { token, profile: EmployeeProfile, status } held in AuthContext; identity/role come from profile.role (EmployeeRole = 'EMPLOYEE' | 'MANAGER' | 'ADMIN') fetched via GET /employees/me, never from JWT decoding. The ApiClient attaches the bearer token from ITokenStorage and clears it on a 401. Route-level access is enforced by the existing RequireAuth guard; action-level visibility is enforced in the page by the status+role matrix (never rendering a forbidden action).
error_response_contract: No new endpoints are exposed by this feature (it consumes the existing backend), so no new error/response contract is introduced. The client surfaces the backend's existing error shape via ApiError: { error: string; code: string } mapped from non-2xx bodies (validation -> 400, auth -> 401, authorization -> 403, not-found -> 404, conflict -> 409). The RequestLeavePage and LeaveDetailPage display ApiError.message (the backend's own error text, e.g. an insufficient-balance message) rather than a generic failure; client-side validation failures (missing dates, end < start, no type) are caught before any network call and shown inline.
